lines.text: KEYPOINTS
Enzymesarebiological ororganiccatalysts.Theyaremadeofproteinsand
can speed up the rate of chemical reactions without themselves being
chemicallychangedattheendofthereactions.
Enzymes are specific in theiractions because of the shape oftheiractive
sites,Only substances with shapes complementaryto that ofactivesite
can fit into theenzymemolecules andbeacted upon bytheenzymes,
Factors affecting the rate of enzyme catalyzed reactions aretemperature,
pH,enzymeconcentration and substrateconcentration.
Every enzyme has its optimum temperature and pH.At optimum
temperatureandpH,anenzymeworksatthegreatestspeed.
When temperature rises well above the optimum temperature, the
protein structure of enzyme is denatured and so the rate of reaction
decreasesrapidly.
Enzymes are specific in action.Theyare specificnot onlyforsubstratebut
alsoforthekindofreaction
Intracellular enzymes e.g.mitochondrial enzymes work inside the cells
while extracellularenzymes e.g.pepsin arereleasedfromthecellandthey
workoutsidethecell.
Cofactors are the non-protein molecules required by enzymes for their
action.
Thecofactors calledprostheticgroups makepermanentattachmentwith
the enzyme while the cofactors called coenzymes are not permanently
attachedtotheenzyme.
An enzyme attaches with the substrate to form enzyme-substrate (ES)
complex.The active site of enzyme catalyzes the reaction and substrate is
convertedtoproduct.
The lockand key model of enzyme action states that the substrate
molecule exactly fits in theactive site of enzyme which is a rigid and non-
flexiblestructure.
Theinducedfitmodelsuggeststhattheenzymemoleculealterstheshape
of active site slightly so that it fits more tightly around the substrate
molecule.
